input: Book a guided cave tour for the upcoming road trip

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: There are many types of guided cave tours — walking, rappelling, spelunking, boat tours — and the type completely changes which caves and operators to look for.
The road trip route or geographic region determines which caves are actually accessible and bookable — a cave in Kentucky is irrelevant if the trip is through the Southwest.
The number of people and their ages/abilities (e.g., young children, seniors, mobility limitations) affects which tour types are suitable and how many tickets to book.
The travel dates narrow the availability window for booking and determine how urgently the reservation needs to be made — some popular caves book out weeks in advance.
The user may prioritize adventure level, scenic beauty, historical/geological significance, or accessibility — this shapes which cave and tour style to prioritize.
Knowing whether the user wants to book directly on the cave's website, through a third-party travel platform, or needs help comparing options determines the immediate next action.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — confirmed reservation in hand, a shortlist of options, or a full itinerary block — defines when this task is actually complete.

gold.taskTitle: Book a guided cave tour for road trip
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to research and book a guided cave tour at some point during an upcoming road trip.

questions.title: What type of cave tour experience are you after?
questions.description: Establish the tour style — e.g., a paved walking tour, a wild spelunking crawl, a boat ride through a cavern, or a lantern-lit historical tour.

questions.title: Which region or route will your road trip cover?
questions.description: Identify the geographic area of the road trip so only caves along the actual route are considered.

questions.title: How many people are going, and are any children or seniors in the group?
questions.description: Determine the group size and any age or mobility factors that would rule out certain tour types or require specific accommodations.

questions.title: What dates are you planning to visit the cave?
questions.description: Pin down the travel window so availability can be checked and booking urgency can be assessed.

questions.title: What matters most to you — adventure level, scenery, or history?
questions.description: Understand the user's priority for the experience to rank and filter cave options appropriately.

questions.title: Where do you prefer to book — the cave's site or a travel platform?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred booking channel to determine the exact next action the user needs to take.

questions.title: What does 'done' look like — a confirmed booking or a shortlist to choose from?
questions.description: Define the finish line for this task so the plan can be scoped correctly.
